Difference between Practices and Skills:
Practices:
1. A practice requires working with other people
1. A practice never stops being built; you never become an expert in a practice, but the behaviors of a practice become more permanent over time
1. A practice is rooted in beliefs and behaviors
1. A practice can be measured through what other people believe about you
1. A practice cannot be concretely measured through deliverables
1. A practice is an intentional choice someone makes to do
1. You learn how to get good about your practice by reflecting to yourself
1. A practice can be measured through what you believe about yourself
1. You learn how to get good about your practice by reflecting with others
Skills:
1. A skill enables you to make a deliverable
1. A skill is measured through how many times you have applied it
1. A skill is rooted in  knowledge and theory
1. A skill applies to a specific activity
1. A skill is expected to be performed in specific job functions
1. A skill is something someone can become an expert in it with a lot of experience
1. A skill you can perform yourself
1. A skill can be practiced by applying it to work you deliver or duties you perform
1. A skill is required in specific jobs, people may not have a choice to perform the skill if the job requires them
1. A skill gets practiced by doing work and performing duties

What they both have in common: 
1. A practice and a skill can be lost if  not continued to be practiced
1. A practice and a skill require willingness to perform
Practice Level 0 Definition:
1. You are not aware of what makes up the practice
1. You are not willing to practice it
1. You tried to practice it, but stopped
Practice Level 1 Definition:
1. You believe it's valuable to practice the practice
1. You are willing to practice it
1. You have knowledge about the components of the practice
1. You've started practicing with others and reflecting
Practice Level 2 Definition:
1. You've seen growth in your own practice through reflection
1. You are starting to work on changing habits
Practice Level 3 Definition:
1. Your habits are starting to become automatic in your practice with others
1. You’re so practiced in it, that you are a role model to others in the practice
1. You can and do advocate for the practice when working with others

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: At its core, Shared Ownership comes from believing a team is stronger when responsibility is spread around. You trust that other people are capable, even when they are still learning, and you are willing to let go of control so they can lead. You also stay honest with yourself about where you can grow, and you treat every teammate's contribution as genuinely valuable.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: In everyday work, this looks like handing off meaningful work instead of hoarding it, and encouraging people who try even when they fall short. You set clear expectations so others can run with the work, admit your own mistakes openly, and make room for teammates to lead on things you could easily have kept for yourself.
Practice Description: Shared Ownership is the idea that the work belongs to everyone on the team, not just whoever was handed a task. When a team practices it, people step up for problems even when they are not officially theirs, and they trust each other to carry real responsibility. It is built from smaller habits like humility, delegation, and a growth mindset, and it deepens over time until sharing the load feels natural. On a healthy team, no one says 'that is not my job.'
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: Empowerment starts with believing that people rise to the trust you place in them. You accept that you do not have all the answers, and that a newer teammate can still produce something great. You value what each person brings, and you would rather someone learn by doing than step in and take over.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: This shows up when you let people solve problems on their own and tell them you believe they can. You recognize effort out loud, even honest attempts that did not work, and you resist the urge to jump in and control the outcome. You listen closely and reflect people's ideas back before adding your own.
Practice Description: Empowerment is about helping the people around you do their best work by trusting them, not managing them. A team that practices it gives people real room to make decisions and figure things out, and treats everyone as capable regardless of title or experience. It grows from habits like letting go of control, listening well, and celebrating effort. The goal is a team where people feel capable and believed in.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: Shared Leadership rests on the belief that everyone can lead and that supporting others is part of your job. You set aside ego and the need to be the smartest person in the room, you assume others hold real wisdom, and you show up as your genuine self instead of performing a role.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: Day to day, this looks like being honest and direct while staying kind, understanding people's needs before acting, and offering steady encouragement. You do not interrupt or dismiss others, you acknowledge where they are right even in disagreement, and you make space for the person best suited to lead in the moment.
Practice Description: Shared Leadership means leadership is something the whole team takes turns holding, not a title one person owns. On a team that practices it, whoever is best suited to guide a given moment steps up, and everyone works to serve the team's success rather than their own status. It is built from qualities like humility, honesty, empathy, and care. The result is a team that can lead itself.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: Psychological Safety comes from believing that everyone belongs and has something worth hearing, even the newest person in the room. You believe people learn by trying and failing, that fresh contributions are welcome no matter someone's experience, and that respectfully challenging the way things work makes the work better.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: In practice, this looks like pausing so quieter voices can speak, listening fully before responding, and sharing your own mistakes and uncertainties so others feel safe to do the same. You invite questions, welcome disagreement, and treat every person as a full member of the team.
Practice Description: Psychological Safety is the shared sense that it is safe to speak up, ask questions, admit mistakes, and challenge ideas without being embarrassed or punished. Research on strong teams, from Amy Edmondson to Google's own studies, points to it as the single biggest factor in how well a team performs. It grows in stages: feeling included, then safe to learn, then safe to contribute, then safe to challenge. When it is present, people bring their whole selves and their best thinking to the work.
Where Can I Learn More?: Amy Edmondson on psychological safety (Harvard, author of The Fearless Organization): https://amycedmondson.com/psychological-safety/

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: Agility rests on the belief that plans are really just guesses that should change as you learn. You would rather figure things out alongside your teammates and your users than perfect a plan on your own, and you treat failure as a fast, useful way to learn what to do next.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: This shows up when you ship small, working results to get real feedback, adjust direction as soon as new information arrives, and help teammates let go of outdated plans. You stay in close contact with customers to find the right path instead of assuming you already know it.
Practice Description: Agility is a way of working that favors learning and adjusting over sticking rigidly to a plan. Rather than trying to answer every question up front, an agile team puts small results in front of real people, learns from the response, and changes course quickly. The idea traces back to the Agile Manifesto and its values, like favoring working results and close collaboration with customers. In short, you make progress by doing, not just by planning.
Where Can I Learn More?: The Agile Manifesto, the founding values of agile work: https://agilemanifesto.org/

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: This practice rests on the belief that the team's combined judgment usually beats any single person's, and that a decision only holds when people have had a genuine say. You stay open to changing a decision when the situation changes, rather than clinging to your first call.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: In everyday work, this looks like gathering input from the group, checking your assumptions out loud, and giving people time to reflect and respond before you lock anything in. You adjust decisions as you learn, and you steer toward a choice the whole team can get behind.
Practice Description: Collective Decision Making is how a team makes choices together so people actually support them, instead of one person deciding for everyone. A team that practices it draws on the knowledge already in the room and gives people time to weigh in before committing. It relies on habits like building consensus, checking assumptions, and staying flexible as situations change. Decisions made this way tend to stick, because the people carrying them out helped shape them.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook

What Mindset Do You Have When You Practi: Continuous Improvement comes from believing that growth is always possible and that failure is a lesson rather than a verdict. You see feedback as a gift that shows you where to get better, and you pay attention to how your own actions affect the people around you.
What Habits Do You Hold When You Practic: This shows up when you regularly step back to reflect on how things went, seek out feedback and act on it instead of getting defensive, and treat fast failures as chances to learn. You watch your own impact on others and make small, steady changes to how you work.
Practice Description: Continuous Improvement is the habit of a team getting a little better all the time by reflecting honestly and acting on what it learns. Instead of repeating the same mistakes, the team treats every sprint and every setback as a chance to adjust how it works. It grows from habits like reflection, self-awareness, seeking feedback, and failing fast. Over time, small improvements add up to a team that keeps getting stronger.
Where Can I Learn More?: Atlassian Team Playbook, practical plays for healthy teamwork: https://www.atlassian.com/team-playbook
